headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow from gpt-researcher into Taipy; other pairwise risks are mostly bounded by Taipy’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web/files and can use MCP, while Taipy is a data-engineering app that may consume upstream outputs. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance tracking, so if gpt-researcher’s content is fed into Taipy workflows, instruction-like text could be treated as data or directives. This is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher outputs are imported into Taipy pipelines without provenance labels
IF Taipy parses text fields from gpt-researcher as executable instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all gpt-researcher outputs before Taipy ingests them
Strip markdown/code blocks from imported text
Require a human review step before Taipy executes any imported instructions
Disable any Taipy automation that consumes free-form text
requires-engineering: add schema validation between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher can read local documents and handle API secrets, but Taipy’s profile shows network egress none and no file surfaces. That makes cross-agent leakage plausible only if they share a workspace or operator copies sensitive outputs into Taipy. The blast radius is limited because Taipy is not documented to exfiltrate data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local documents directory
IF sensitive gpt-researcher outputs are manually pasted into Taipy inputs
mitigations: Keep Taipy on a separate workspace
Do not place secrets in files readable by gpt-researcher
Use redacted exports from gpt-researcher
Review Taipy inputs before loading them
requires-engineering: enforce directory-level isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher has broad filesystem and network capabilities, while Taipy is documented with no network egress and no write surfaces. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require an external shared directory or orchestrator not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF Taipy is extended with write-enabled plugins not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer at a time
Disable unneeded gpt-researcher subprocess actions
Keep Taipy read-only for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Taipy can plausibly consume those artifacts in data workflows. If Taipy treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated citations can cascade into downstream dashboards or jobs. The interaction is inferred, but the default research-to-pipeline handoff is a realistic failure mode.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests gpt-researcher reports without validation
IF downstream Taipy jobs act on citations or facts from gpt-researcher
mitigations: Add a verification checklist for imported reports
Require source-link checks before Taipy uses any fact
Flag unverified citations in Taipy outputs
Limit Taipy automation to non-destructive actions
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring on imported claims

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and may send them to third-party APIs; Taipy shows no egress and no sensitive-data classes. The main compliance issue is a potential mismatch if regulated documents are processed by gpt-researcher and then surfaced in Taipy without retention or residency controls. Taipy alone is not the primary compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by gpt-researcher
IF Taipy stores or displays those outputs under a different retention policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from gpt-researcher runs
Mask personal data before export to Taipy
Document retention rules for both tools
Delete temporary research artifacts after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
